text: I inherited the farm leadership from my father.
He died during a poor harvest year.
That year people argued more than they worked.
I learned early that blame spreads faster than crops grow.
The terrace fields were already old when I took over.
No one remembers who first cut them into the hillside.
They still hold water, which is what matters.
The channels from the hill streams sometimes shift after heavy rains.
We repair them every season.
If we don't, the terraces fail quickly.
I've seen strange carvings on the irrigation stonework upstream, near the old channel head.
Satyapala says the forest hides older paths.
I don't have time to chase that.
The temple asks for offerings at the harvest festival, for Sita's blessing on the furrows.
I don't object, as long as it doesn't delay planting.
Nara once said the grain is 'blessed.'
I don't know what that means in practical terms.
The ash-year from Kalinga cracked several of the granary walls.
After that year, the grain shortages lasted longer than expected.
People still argue about what caused it.
I blame poor planning and a bad monsoon.
But I don't say that loudly at temple gatherings.
Somadatta spends too much time listening to Senaka's stories.
I worry he'll get distracted from real work.
Marisha believes we should store more grain than the old custom allows.
She's usually right.
Balamitra trusts the system too much.
Systems fail under pressure.
I've seen it before.
The hills always take back what people assume is stable.
